desks.Dividends: Microsoft goes ex Thu Nov 19 at $0.98, the raised quarterly rate declared Sep 15, its 24th consecutive annual increase — the only declared watchlist ex-date in the window. Apple's Nov 10 date is UNVERIFIED and undeclared: one source lists it, Nasdaq, Zacks, and Yahoo do not. Nvidia's next dividend is undeclared, SPY and QQQ point to mid-to-late December on pattern only, Tesla pays no dividend, and no cuts or specials were found.
desks.Earnings: Microsoft Wed Oct 28 after close (webcast 5:30 p.m. ET) is the week's binary event, on FOMC day, with a reported implied move of about 4.9–5.3% either way. Apple Mon Nov 2 after close (call 5:00 p.m. ET) follows with a reported implied move of about 4.1–5.7%, depending on expiry and method. Reported consensus, not independently verified: Microsoft about $4.71–4.73 per share on about $90.6 billion revenue; Apple $2.00 per share on $112.95 billion revenue. Tesla already reported Oct 21; Nvidia's date is UNVERIFIED, with trackers split between Nov 17 and 18, outside the window.
desks.Futures: Crude is pricing a Middle East shipping risk premium, not a confirmed supply shortfall: Brent $116.26 and WTI $102.16 intraday Oct 27, with Hormuz flows at about 60% of normal per ANZ research cited by Reuters and the Brent–WTI spread widening to $14.05 on Oct 26. The last EIA print showed a third straight crude draw of 3.1 million barrels to 412.5 million, with distillates 9% below the five-year average. Natural gas storage rose 77 Bcf to 3,644 Bcf. Next catalysts: EIA petroleum Wed Oct 28, EIA gas Thu Oct 29, OPEC+ Sun Nov 1, WASDE Tue Nov 10.
desks.Parity: No published put-call or box parity violation was found; VIX options parity forwards of 19.17 (Nov 18) and 19.20 (Dec 16) sit close to VIX futures at 19.120 and 19.170. The methodology item to watch is the S&P Dow Jones Indices growth/value revamp, with momentum dropping out of growth scoring and free cash flow, forward earnings, and intangible assets entering the value screens, before the open Mon Dec 21. The reported passive exposure of $375 billion or more is an analyst estimate, not an S&P figure. S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi also announced a preferred-provider agreement Oct 26.
desks.Premium: Microsoft's Oct 30 at-the-money implied volatility is 60.9% against 19.5% 20-day realized volatility — event pricing ahead of tomorrow's earnings, not a mispricing read, with the term structure falling to 48.7% for Nov 2. SPY (11.6% vs 9.7% realized), QQQ (18.0% vs 18.8%), and Tesla (30.0% vs 34.0%) sit near realized on the front expiry. Apple, Nvidia, and QQQ reads are window-contingent (single-day variance shares of 36.4%, 31.0%, and 32.0%), so no clean verdict is issued for those three. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names; no free IV-history source was available.
desks.Quant lab: Eleven candidates were scored and appended to the ledger (#157–167), none reaching TEST or INTEGRATE. Four sit in the WATCH band: an FX walk-forward evaluation harness (#167, score 49, the sweep's highest), an implied-volatility surface survey paper (#157, 46), an IV surface builder with tests and CI (#162, 46), and a Dupire calibration repo valued for its certificate pattern (#163, 45). headline: Daily research brief — Tuesday, October 27

items.detail: The FOMC decision lands Wed Oct 28 at 2:00 p.m. ET (press conference 2:30 p.m. ET), and Microsoft reports after the close the same day. Microsoft's front implied volatility is 60.9% against 19.5% 20-day realized volatility — the market is pricing the event, not a mispricing. Premium into it carries event risk plus post-print implied-volatility crush, and the Oct 29 session move cannot be attributed to earnings alone.
items.title: Wednesday pairs the Fed decision with Microsoft earnings

items.detail: Apple reports Mon Nov 2 after close, with a call at 5:00 p.m. ET. Its priced move is about 4–6%, depending on expiry and method — a wide range, not a single number, and it should not be collapsed to one. Over Apple's last five reports the signed mean move was -1.3% and the mean absolute move 2.8%, so direction has not been predictable from the earnings print alone.
items.title: Apple earnings follow Monday, with a wide priced range

items.detail: Microsoft, ex Thu Nov 19 at $0.98 per quarter (pay Dec 10), is the only declared watchlist dividend event in the window, and the $0.98 rate is the Sep 15 board raise executing — its 24th consecutive annual increase. Apple's expected Nov 10 dividend is UNVERIFIED and undeclared as of this run: one source lists it, while Nasdaq, Zacks, and Yahoo do not. Do not book Nov 10 as fact.
items.title: Only one declared dividend in the window

items.detail: FRED prints as of Mon Oct 26 put the effective fed funds rate at 3.88%, the 2-year at 4.68%, and the 10-year at 5.00%, a 2s10s spread of +32 basis points, with SOFR 5 basis points over the effective fed funds rate. That is calm funding, no inversion, and no rates-driven volatility regime change. The 10-year is up 27 basis points over 60 days, a higher discount-rate bar for distant cash flows, not a mispricing signal.
items.title: Rates are calm but higher into the Fed decision
